introduction_markdown: You are required to answer FIVE questions, choosing THREE from Section A and TWO from Section B. All the questions carry equal marks allocated to parts of questions are indicated. Extra questions answered from each section shall NOT be marked. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers. Duration: two and a half hours.
incertitudes: Le PDF a 3 pages (page de garde, Section A, Section B), toutes lues en image ; rien ne manque. Filigranes et publicites ignores. Identite verifiee : Ordinary Level, juin 2019, Human Biology, Paper 2, code 0565, deux heures et demie.

Choix : la page de garde impose de repondre a 5 questions, 3 parmi la Section A (questions 1 a 5) et 2 parmi la Section B (questions 6 a 9). Traduit en regles_choix : SECTION A 3 sur 5, SECTION B 2 sur 4 (identique dans tous les fichiers). La phrase imprimee « All the questions carry equal marks allocated to parts of questions are indicated » est recopiee telle quelle (sans ponctuation entre marks et allocated).

Le sujet imprime les points par sous-partie en fin de question (ex. « (7, 5, 8 marks) ») ; ils sont repartis ici sur les sous-questions dans le meme ordre, sans rien corriger. Les 9 questions totalisent 20 points avec ces valeurs imprimees.
Le sujet ne contient aucune figure. Les schemas demandes au candidat sont decrits dans le corrige, sans figure.

questions.enonce_markdown: In tabular form, differentiate between mitosis and meiosis. *(8 marks)*
questions.corrige_markdown:
| Mitosis | Meiosis |
|---|---|
| Occurs in **body (somatic) cells**, for growth, repair and asexual reproduction | Occurs in the **reproductive organs** (testes and ovaries) to form **gametes** |
| **One division** | **Two successive divisions** (meiosis I and meiosis II) |
| Produces **two daughter cells** | Produces **four daughter cells** |
| Daughter cells have the **same chromosome number as the parent (diploid, 2n)** | Daughter cells have **half the chromosome number (haploid, n)** |
| Daughter cells are **genetically identical** to the parent cell | Daughter cells are **genetically different** (variation) |
| **No pairing of homologous chromosomes** (no bivalents) | **Homologous chromosomes pair up** to form bivalents |
| **No crossing over** | **Crossing over** (chiasmata) occurs between chromatids |
| Does not produce variation | Produces variation (crossing over and independent assortment) |

questions.enonce_markdown: Draw a large and neatly labelled diagram of the lateral view of the male reproductive system. *(6 marks)*
questions.corrige_markdown:
*Diagram to be drawn by the candidate: a large, side view (sagittal section) of the male pelvic region, drawn in pencil with ruled label lines, and a title (e.g. "Lateral view of the male reproductive system").*

**What to draw:** the **urinary bladder** at the top, with the **ureter** entering it; below it the **prostate gland**, surrounding the start of the **urethra**; the **seminal vesicle** behind the bladder, joining the **vas deferens (sperm duct)** that comes up from the testis and loops over the ureter; the **urethra** running down through the **penis** to its opening; the **penis** with the **glans penis** covered by the **foreskin**; the **Cowper's (bulbourethral) gland** below the prostate; the **scrotum** hanging below the penis and holding the **testis**, with the coiled **epididymis** lying against it; the **rectum and anus** behind, and the **pubic bone** in front.

**Labels expected:** bladder, ureter, seminal vesicle, prostate gland, Cowper's gland, vas deferens, urethra, penis, glans penis, foreskin, testis, epididymis, scrotum, rectum, anus.

questions.enonce_markdown: State the secondary sexual characteristics of human males. *(6 marks)*
questions.corrige_markdown:
At puberty, the male hormone **testosterone** (from the testes) causes the following **secondary sexual characteristics**:

1. **Growth of hair** on the face (beard and moustache), in the armpits, on the chest and in the pubic region.
2. The **voice deepens (breaks)** because the larynx enlarges (Adam's apple).
3. **Broadening of the shoulders** and **development of muscles** (a muscular body).
4. **Increased growth in height** and body mass.
5. **Enlargement of the penis and testes**, and the beginning of the production of sperm.
6. The skin becomes **oily**, which may cause acne.
7. Changes in behaviour (more aggressive, interest in the opposite sex).
